AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To investigate the feasibility of implementing a video-game exercise programme for older people with chronic low back pain (LBP).

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: Physiotherapy outpatient department in a public hospital in Western Sydney, Australia.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: We will recruit 60 participants over 55 years old with chronic LBP from the waiting list.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTIONS
AbstractText.content: Participants will be randomised to receive video-game exercise (n=30) or to remain on the waiting list (n=30) for 8 weeks, with follow up at 3 and 6 months. Participants engaging in video-game exercises will be unsupervised and will complete video-game exercise for 60minutes, 3 times per week. Participants allocated to remain on the waiting list will be encouraged to maintain their usual levels of physical activity.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE
AbstractText.content: The primary outcomes for this feasibility study will be study processes (recruitment and response rates, adherence to and experience with the intervention, and incidence of adverse events) relevant to the future design of a large RCT. Estimates of treatment efficacy (point estimates and 95% confidence intervals) on pain self-efficacy, care seeking, physical activity, fear of movement/re-injury, pain, physical function, disability, falls-efficacy, strength, and walking speed, will be our secondary outcome measures.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Recruitment for this trial began in November 2015.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: This study describes the rationale and processes of a feasibility study investigating a video-game exercise programme for older people with chronic LBP. Results from the feasibility study will inform on the design and sample required for a large multicentre RCT.

AbstractText.Label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
AbstractText.content: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry: ACTRN12615000703505.
